hook_text: An eggbeater handle turns one way and the beaters spin another. Gears on cones make the turn.
clip_script: Spur gears need parallel shafts. Cut the teeth on cones instead and set two cones point to point: now the shafts meet at 90 degrees. That is a bevel pair. Same maths as before, driven teeth over driver teeth. Equal gears: 1 to 1, just round the corner. Small pinion driving a big crown wheel: slower and stronger, the back axle of a bakkie. Big wheel driving a small pinion: faster and weaker, the hand drill. Eggbeater, angle grinder, windmill pump, all bevel pairs. Nothing new in the numbers. Only the angle changed.
visual_style: Whiteboard cones point to point with teeth; shafts at right angles with arrows; a bakkie axle with a big crown wheel and a small pinion; a hand drill; the ratio formula repeated.
mood: Confident and neat, like a kitchen demonstration.
pacing: Eggbeater, cones, right angle, ratio, bakkie, drill, nothing new.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look inside a hand drill or eggbeater to find the bevel pair.
